provider: jsDelivr as the free CDN layer over GitHub repos

free_tier.stated: free for personal and commercial use with no limits on bandwidth or number of requests; GitHub-proxy soft limits of 10 000 actively accessed files and 100 000 files per repository
free_tier.notes: the acceptable-use-policy URL serves the jsDelivr Terms of Use, effective October 5, 2026; the file-count soft limits are not automatically enforced

per_object_cap.stated: We actually allow files up to 20 MB for GitHub regardless of the overall repo size
per_object_cap.notes: We actually allow files up to 20 MB for GitHub regardless of the overall repo size

retention.stated: Previously served immutable files may be retained in permanent storage even after upstream deletion. We do not accept removal requests simply because a package or version was unpublished, deleted upstream, or is no longer needed.
retention.notes: We use a permanent S3 storage to ensure all files remain available even if GitHub goes down or a repository or a release is deleted by its author.

limits_note: Git repo files only — release assets are NOT served (probed: /gh/cli/cli@v2.102.1/dist/README.md -> 404). ~20 MB effective per-file ceiling for the GitHub proxy (the git-unlimited-storage README states 'jsDelivr per file | 20 MB'); hard per-file/per-package caps are undocumented and enforced at request time. Does not serve the >2 GiB release assets, so the serving path for big objects stays on GitHub's own Fastly edge.

notes: Provides CDN distribution rather than origin storage. Documentation states 'there are no limits on bandwidth or number of requests' (AUP section 1), with soft limits of 10,000 actively accessed files and 100,000 files per repository.

extras.verified_at_basis: checked against the live service on 2026-11-09
extras.quota_verbatim: Not storage, it is the egress answer for the serving workload: "there are no limits on bandwidth or number of requests" (AUP section 1), with soft limits of 10,000 actively accessed files and 100,000 files per repository.
extras.limits_verbatim: Git repo files only — release assets are NOT served (probed: /gh/cli/cli@v2.102.1/dist/README.md -> 404). ~20 MB effective per-file ceiling for the GitHub proxy (the git-unlimited-storage README states 'jsDelivr per file | 20 MB'); hard per-file/per-package caps are undocumented and enforced at request time. Does not serve the >2 GiB release assets, so the serving path for big objects stays on GitHub's own Fastly edge.
extras.egress_verbatim: Unmetered, and immutable-cached at the edge: probed 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, s-maxage=31536000, immutable' plus Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. This cleanly covers the 500 GB-1 TiB/day serving workload from a single repo without touching GitHub's own edge.
extras.chaining_verbatim: Serving layer only: pair it with Releases (storage) or a git repo (small files). One repo backs 1 TiB/day because the edge absorbs repeats with a 1-year immutable TTL.
extras.tooling_verbatim: URL pattern https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/USER/REPO@TAG/path — no client needed, no auth, no config. Purge API exists for cache busting.
extras.agent_focus: GitHub as storage — quantitative ceilings (per-file / per-release / per-repo / per-account), multiplication model, and the automation layer (gh, oras, softprops, gh-large-releases, cf-github-releases, jsDelivr)

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
